source_event_id: share-<grant_id>-<sha256(address)[:12]> — keyed to the INVITE (the grant) and the address, never to the address alone: a redelivery dedupes at the intake, while inviting the same person again mints a new grant and mails again, which is what pressing Invite twice means. The address is hashed so the id carries none.
description: A meeting's owner invited ONE address from the terminal's Share dialog and asked for the mail; triggers meeting_share, whose one step mints that person's own restricted link at send time — as the owner, through meeting-api's share mint — and mails it. PUBLISHED BY MEETING-API (meeting_api/events.py, the existing publish-edge) from the by-id share mint, only when the body says notify, only for a grant restricted to exactly one address, and under a per-owner hourly cap; the post-meeting attendee fan-out mints its own grants and mails them itself, so it never double-mails. NO CREDENTIAL TRAVELS: `grant_id` names the owner's grant for the record, and the link is minted where it is sent, so the event store never holds a working token (meeting-api keeps grants as hashes at rest). `uid` is the OWNER, the subject `_global` is read through and the identity the link is minted as; the recipient is `email`. `title` (bounded, one line of plain text) and `inviter` are words for the mail and may be empty.
